profiles.windows: Windows PowerShell 5.1 on each sampled device. Use elevation for machine settings; run user-policy checks as the test user.
profiles.graph: PowerShell 7; Microsoft.Graph.Authentication. Connect-MgGraph -TenantId <tenant-GUID> -Scopes <permissions listed in the check> -NoWelcome. Verify Get-MgContext, then Disconnect-MgGraph after use. Examples use commercial-cloud Graph v1.0.
profiles.exchange: PowerShell 7; ExchangeOnlineManagement. Connect-ExchangeOnline -UserPrincipalName <auditor-UPN>. Verify Get-ConnectionInformation. Use Exchange roles exposing the listed read cmdlets; finish with Disconnect-ExchangeOnline.
profiles.purview: ExchangeOnlineManagement; Connect-IPPSSession -UserPrincipalName <auditor-UPN>. Use DLP read roles or Audit Reader/View-Only Audit Logs as applicable; retention-policy access needs the relevant audit role.
profiles.sharepoint: Windows PowerShell 5.1; Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell. Connect-SPOService -Url https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com with a SharePoint Administrator.
profiles.teams: MicrosoftTeams module; Connect-MicrosoftTeams -TenantId <tenant-GUID> with policy read access.
profiles.azure: PowerShell 7; Az.Accounts and the Az modules used below. Connect-AzAccount -Tenant <tenant-GUID>; Set-AzContext -Subscription <subscription-GUID>. Use Reader plus the required service/data-plane read role. Repeat for every scoped subscription.
profiles.ad: Windows PowerShell 5.1; Import-Module ActiveDirectory (RSAT). Query the intended domain/DC. Run local DC registry, service and SMB checks in an elevated session on each DC.
profiles.csv: Use UTF-8 CSV exports with the listed columns and UTC timestamps. Reconcile row counts and scope to the source system before running.
profiles.power: Windows PowerShell 5.1; Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell and its dependencies. Add-PowerAppsAccount with Power Platform administrator access.
profiles.devops: PowerShell 7 or 5.1; short-lived Azure DevOps PAT with Code (read) and Build (read). Enter it as the Get-Credential password; revoke it after use.
profiles.dns: Windows PowerShell with the DnsClient module; ordinary DNS read access.

run_steps: Sample managed endpoints and exception groups. Export Intune device status or resultant GPO; record policy ID, version and targeted users/devices.

WDAC: on Windows 11 22H2+/Server 2025, run CiTool and match the organisation policy IDs. Check source XML for option 3 (Enabled:Audit Mode), UMCI and script settings; confirm load event 3099. On older Windows, use policy XML and CodeIntegrity events.

AppLocker GPO/local policy: export effective XML and inspect applicable EXE, DLL, MSI, Script and Appx collections, enforcement mode, bypass rules and AppIDSvc. For CSP/MDM deployments, obtain ApplicationLaunchRestrictions XML and device status from MDM instead.

Prepare approved and unapproved harmless files; record hashes. As a standard test user, launch both in a representative test environment. Repeat for required scripts, installers and DLLs. Test-AppLockerPolicy predicts a decision; it does not execute the file.

Match runtime results to events: WDAC 3077 blocks, 3076 audits; AppLocker EXE/DLL 8002 allows, 8003 audits, 8004 blocks. MSI/Script uses 8005/8006/8007. WDAC script events 8028/8029 indicate audit/enforcement; check actual PowerShell Constrained Language behaviour.
Verify central event delivery. Retain policy/MDM exports, fixture hashes, user/device details and observed results for each policy combination.
TECH-APP-CONTROL.decision: Approved files run; unapproved files are blocked or constrained as required by the enforced policy, with matching local and central events.
TECH-APP-CONTROL.limits: CiTool IsEnforced means active, not necessarily deny mode. Get-AppLockerPolicy cannot retrieve CSP policy. Test each required file type; a driver-only policy does not cover applications.

TECH-MAIL-AUTH.command:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$domain = Read-Host 'An organisation-owned mail domain (no @)'
if ($domain -notmatch '^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$') { throw 'Enter a DNS domain.' }
Resolve-DnsName -Name $domain -Type TXT
Resolve-DnsName -Name ('_dmarc.'+$domain) -Type TXT
$dkim = Get-DkimSigningConfig -Identity $domain
$dkim | Select-Object Domain,Enabled,Status,Selector1CNAME,Selector2CNAME
Resolve-DnsName -Name ('selector1._domainkey.'+$domain) -Type CNAME
Resolve-DnsName -Name ('selector2._domainkey.'+$domain) -Type CNAME
run_steps: Inventory sending domains and services. Check SPF, active DKIM selectors and DMARC policy/report destinations.
Send a tagged message through each approved sender. Inspect SPF/DKIM results and alignment in the received headers.
Use an owned test domain to exercise an unauthorised sender path; check rejection/quarantine and reports.
TECH-MAIL-AUTH.decision: Approved senders authenticate and align; the unauthorised test receives the intended DMARC action.
TECH-MAIL-AUTH.limits: Recipient policy can override DMARC handling; record the actual receiving system and result.
